title: Refactor listener/pipeline.py from monolithic run() into segmented stages that dispatch Telegram between each step (operator 2026-09-16: 'TG#1 should be sent before anything is called for VM2')
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-16, post the Ford F-150 alert miss)
trigger: Operator 2026-09-16 (verbatim): 'OK, well then you deliberately broke something in the system. Telegram message one should be sent before anything is called and any action is taken for VM two. That pipeline, I designed specifically to be able to address this type of issue. It shouldn't be a single monolithic pipeline. Is supposed to be segmented calls out to different modules of the pipeline With telegram notifications and decisions made between each step.' Confirmed by 2026-09-16 morning audit: 6 confirmed-tg events (10:14-10:20, including Ford F-150 truck at 10:19:49) all silently dropped because listener/pipeline.py::run() raises ValueError at telegram_formatter/detail.py:184 BEFORE returning to daemon.py:276, which means daemon never dispatches ANY of tg1/tg2/tg3 even though tg1 was successfully built at stage 9. Spec says 'TG#1 fires' (item 7) then 'VM2' (item 8) then 'TG#2 fires' (item 9). Current code builds all three then dispatches all three from daemon AFTER run() returns -- an exception at stage 11 unwinds the entire function. Last successful Telegram send: 2026-09-15 14:12:54 (~20 hours of silence at the time of operator report). The fix is to segment the pipeline into discrete stage calls, dispatch each TG message immediately after its stage, and let per-stage try/except boundaries contain failures so earlier TGs already-sent stay sent.
background: Current state in /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/listener/pipeline.py:108-261 (run() function): 12-stage monolithic sequence. Stages 3-13 all run inside ONE function call. Stages 9+ (vm1, build TG#1, vm2, build TG#2, match, build TG#3) ALL execute before any Telegram is dispatched. Stage 11 build_detail_message raises ValueError when vm2_result lacks 'class_confirmed'/'class' keys (telegram_formatter/detail.py:184 -- fails for mode-specific VM2 outputs: vehicle->make/color/body_style_hint/model, person->attributes, animal->species). When the raise fires, the function unwinds with no return value; daemon.py:276 catches the exception and returns HTTP 500 to the camera. TG#1 (built in memory at stage 9) is discarded along with everything else. Daemon's dispatch loop (daemon.py:283-356) only reads result['tg1','tg2','tg3'] AFTER pipeline.run() returns. Spec says each TG fires IMMEDIATELY after its stage (docs/PIPELINE-SPEC-2026-09-10.md items 7, 9, 11). The architecture violates the spec by batching. Fix: segment the pipeline into named stage functions, move dispatch into the daemon's per-stage loop, add per-stage try/except boundaries so later failures cannot kill earlier TGs already-sent.
goal: listener/pipeline.py exports a bag of named, testable stage functions (one per stage). listener/daemon.py orchestrates them in a per-stage loop, dispatching each Telegram message IMMEDIATELY after its producing stage. A failure at any stage N+1 (e.g., VM2 returns malformed output, match raises) does NOT unwind TG#N that was already sent. record_hit() fires ONLY after TG#3 successfully dispatches (spec item 12). Each stage function is independently testable with no monkey-patching of pipeline.run(). Daemon returns HTTP 200 even on stage failure (existing behavior preserved: camera-side retry storm avoidance per US-022b).

operator_guarantees.no_residue: After all stories land: listener/pipeline.py exports individual stage functions named stage_load_frames, stage_gate, stage_cooldown_check, stage_prepare_artifacts, stage_verify_class_vm1, stage_build_tg1, stage_detail_class_vm2, stage_build_tg2, stage_perform_match, stage_build_tg3. The monolithic run() function is DELETED (US-050e). No callsite of pipeline.run() remains (verified by grep). No inline TG#3 send_match_alert call inside pipeline.py (it moves to daemon).
operator_guarantees.dispatch_order: In listener/daemon.py: the /alert route calls stage functions in order: stage_load_frames -> stage_gate -> stage_cooldown_check -> stage_prepare_artifacts -> stage_verify_class_vm1 -> stage_build_tg1 + dispatcher.dispatch([tg1]) -> stage_detail_class_vm2 -> stage_build_tg2 + dispatcher.dispatch([tg2]) -> stage_perform_match -> stage_build_tg3 + dispatcher.dispatch([tg3]) -> record_hit(). Each dispatch fires BEFORE the next stage runs.
operator_guarantees.tg1_survives_vm2_failure: If stage_detail_class_vm2 raises OR stage_build_tg2 raises, TG#1 has already been dispatched. Daemon logs the failure, returns HTTP 200 to camera, but does NOT send TG#2 or TG#3 and does NOT record_hit(). Verified by test in tests/test_pipeline_segmented.py::test_tg1_dispatched_when_stage_detail_class_raises.
operator_guarantees.no_inline_send: grep proves: telegram_formatter/match_alert.py::send_match_alert is NOT called from inside any pipeline.py or any stage function. It is called only from listener/daemon.py in the per-stage loop. No other inline httpx.Client or send_match_alert call survives outside the dispatcher.
operator_guarantees.contract_fix: After US-050d: telegram_formatter/detail.py::build_detail_message no longer raises ValueError on mode-specific outputs. The function accepts each mode's specific key set (vehicle->make/color/body_style_hint/model/vehicle_features, person->attributes, animal->species) and produces mode-appropriate captions. infra/vision_analyzer.py::detail_class with mode='unsure' is handled (returns a structured 'unsure' dict instead of raising).
operator_guarantees.cooldown_correctness: record_hit() fires ONLY in the daemon's per-stage loop, AFTER dispatcher.dispatch([tg3]) returns success. If TG#3 dispatch fails or any earlier stage failed, record_hit is NOT called -- so the next alert on the same camera within the cooldown window is correctly suppressed. Verified by test test_cooldown_not_recorded_when_stage_build_tg2_raises.
operator_guarantees.tests_clean: tests/test_pipeline_segmented.py is the new test file (replaces assertions that depended on the monolithic run() returning a dict with all three tgs). Existing tests that patched pipeline.run() are updated to patch the individual stage functions instead. test_pipeline.py still exists for vehicle matcher scoring (it doesn't touch the pipeline module).
operator_guarantees.no_defensive_fallbacks: Per operator 2026-09-15: 'I never ever ever want a defensive fallback.' Per-stage try/except blocks exist ONLY for the dispatch call (so a Telegram API hiccup doesn't surface as HTTP 5xx to camera per US-022b contract). Stage-level failures (VM2 returns malformed output, match raises) re-raise to the per-stage boundary; they are NOT silently swallowed with a default fallback. No 'send what we have' logic in the catch block.
operator_guarantees.ascii_only: No Unicode, em-dashes, or smart quotes in any file the PRD touches.
operator_guarantees.v1_refactor_out_of_scope: Same monolithic architecture exists in /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-refactor/ (NOT under this PRD's scope). v2 is the canonical surface; the refactor repo is operator-driven and out of scope.

shipping_definition: (a) Operator runs the daemon for 24+ hours with the segmented pipeline applied. (b) logs/daemon.log shows 'tg-send:' lines for TG#1 firing IMMEDIATELY after stage_verify_class_vm1 -- BEFORE any 'httpx POST localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions' (VM2) line in the same alert's trace. (c) Trigger a real VM2 failure (e.g., kill the VM2 llama-server mid-flight): TG#1 still arrives at Telegram within the alert's normal window. (d) All 7 stories merged to main, ACs verified by their respective workers, no dangling worktrees.

stories.notes: The spec at docs/PIPELINE-SPEC-2026-09-10.md items 8 and 9 already says VM2 returns mode-specific fields (vehicle->license plate/features/color/type, person->clothing/height/identity markers, animal->species/color/markings).
